newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end firmer, platinum weaker.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end firmer, platinum weaker.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended slightly firmer on Tuesday, recovering from early lows as the yen's weakness stimulated sporadic buying, while platinum prices settled mostly weaker, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from unchanged to four yen per gram firmer. Most-active benchmark August was two yen firmer at 1,344 yen.

The gold market was supported by indications that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) may not reach an agreement on gold sales soon. Bullion was quoted at $383.20/50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $383.00/40 in New York on Monday.
In the spot gold market, a delayed decision on IMF gold sales is likely to fuel a technical rally led by short-covering in the short term, the traders said.
But expected selling by Australian producers, taking advantage of rises in Australian dollar-based gold price, could put a lid on further gold price rallies, the traders added.
In lacklustre trade in gold futures, private investors built fresh long positions in distant months, based on views that the yen will fall further against the dollar.
Platinum futures ranged from six yen per gram lower to one yen firmer. Benchmark August was flat at 1,364 yen.
In the platinum futures market, active buying by one commodity brokerage house was detected, while trade houses sold futures while buying spot platinum in arbitrage trade.
Spot platinum was quoted at $388.00/389.00 at the Tokyo close, supported by Japanese trade houses' buying, against $387.50/388.50 at the Tokyo open.
"Spot platinum remains vulnerable to downside risks," one trader said.
Silver futures were mixed, while palladium futures slipped. Benchmark August silver was 0.2 yen per 10 grams weaker at 181.1 yen. Benchmark August palladium was down four yen at 431.
